candidates.name: Dumbbell Overhead Carry

distinctFrom.why: load locked out overhead rather than hanging at the side; sustained overhead shoulder stability replaces the anti-lateral-flexion demand of a side carry

sources: NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (strongman/carry and Olympic-lift chapters)
candidates.notes: exerciseType is distance or time, not weight_reps (no "distance" exerciseType exists in the current schema — see vocabulary-gap note in the top-level report); rep fields left null.

candidates.name: Dumbbell Front Rack Carry

distinctFrom.why: two dumbbells racked at the shoulders rather than hanging at the sides; the anti-flexion demand moves from the grip/lats to the upper trunk holding the rack position

sources: Established S&C coaching literature (strongman conditioning texts, USAW technical manual for the Olympic-lift derivatives)
candidates.notes: exerciseType distance or time, not weight_reps.

candidates.name: Trap Bar Carry

distinctFrom.why: implement family differs (a single trap bar with fixed handle width vs two independently spaced dumbbells)

sources: NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (strongman/carry and Olympic-lift chapters)
candidates.notes: Trap bar has no dedicated coarse equipment value in this vocabulary; tagged "barbell", matching the existing "Trap Bar Deadlift" and "Trap Bar Shrug" rows. exerciseType distance or time, not weight_reps.

candidates.name: Barbell Zercher Carry

distinctFrom.why: the bar is walked rather than squatted; the movement pattern is carry, not squat, even though the hold is identical

sources: Established S&C coaching literature (strongman conditioning texts, USAW technical manual for the Olympic-lift derivatives)
candidates.notes: exerciseType distance or time, not weight_reps. Bar held in the crook of the elbows against the torso.

candidates.name: Dumbbell Waiter's Carry

distinctFrom.why: the dumbbell is balanced upright on an open palm rather than gripped by the handle; wrist and finger stabilisation replace a closed-grip hold

sources: Established S&C coaching literature (strongman conditioning texts, USAW technical manual for the Olympic-lift derivatives)
candidates.notes: exerciseType distance or time, not weight_reps. Light-load balance drill; the open-palm hold is the whole coaching point.

candidates.name: Sled Row

distinctFrom.why: the lifter stands still and pulls the sled toward themselves hand-over-hand on a rope, rather than walking backward or forward while attached

sources: Established S&C coaching literature (strongman conditioning texts, USAW technical manual for the Olympic-lift derivatives)
candidates.notes: exerciseType time or distance-of-rope-pulled, not weight_reps; new coarse equipment value "sled" used per this campaign’s vocabulary (the existing Sled Push/Pull/Prowler Drag rows predate it and stay tagged "machine"). "sled" is not yet in the demands.js SINGLE_IMPLEMENT/FIXED_IMPLEMENT sets, so grip/unilateral/bilateral axes derive null; overridden here from the mechanics (one shared sled load, cannot be split per side).

candidates.name: Sled Reverse Drag

distinctFrom.why: walked backward facing away from the sled with straps over the shoulders, rather than facing the sled and pulling it forward hand-over-hand or by harness

sources: Established S&C coaching literature (strongman conditioning texts, USAW technical manual for the Olympic-lift derivatives)
candidates.notes: exerciseType distance or time, not weight_reps. Knee-extension-dominant compared to the hip-hinge-dominant forward Sled Pull. "sled" equipment not yet in demands.js implement sets, so grip/bilateral axes derive null; overridden from the mechanics (harness/straps, hands are not the load-bearing interface).

candidates.name: Sled Lateral Drag

distinctFrom.why: side-stepping drag with the harness/strap attached to the hip, loading the frontal-plane hip abductors/adductors rather than the sagittal-plane hip extensors

sources: Established S&C coaching literature (strongman conditioning texts, USAW technical manual for the Olympic-lift derivatives)
candidates.notes: exerciseType distance or time, not weight_reps. Same "sled" implement-set gap as Sled Row/Sled Reverse Drag; overridden the same way.

candidates.name: Medicine Ball Chest Pass

distinctFrom.why: a two-hand explosive throw released away from the chest (resistance/power work) rather than a held anti-rotation twist

sources: NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (strongman/carry and Olympic-lift chapters)
candidates.notes: Ballistic per EL-7 (throw); when-in-doubt-safer-tier applied (never_auto), matching the caution EL-5 gives kettlebell ballistics, since the release/catch cycle carries the same risk-profile logic. "medicine_ball" is not yet in demands.js implement sets, so several axes derive null; overridden from the mechanics below.

candidates.name: Medicine Ball Rotational Throw

distinctFrom.why: implement family differs (medicine ball released against a wall vs a fixed landmine bar) and the ball is thrown, not held through a controlled rotation

sources: NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (strongman/carry and Olympic-lift chapters)
candidates.notes: Ballistic per EL-7 (throw); never_auto, when-in-doubt-safer-tier. "medicine_ball" implement-set gap as above; axialLoad false to match the corpus’s own convention for rotation-pattern movements (e.g. "Landmine Rotation"), which are not treated as axial despite the trunk torque.

candidates.name: Medicine Ball Slam

distinctFrom.why: new movement family for this corpus: overhead-to-floor explosive slam, none of the seeded rows perform it

sources: NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (strongman/carry and Olympic-lift chapters)
Established S&C coaching literature (strongman conditioning texts, USAW technical manual for the Olympic-lift derivatives)
candidates.notes: Ballistic per EL-7 (throw/slam is the throw family); never_auto. "medicine_ball" implement-set gap as above.

candidates.name: Medicine Ball Overhead Throw

distinctFrom.why: thrown forward or backward through an overhead arc and released, rather than driven down into the floor in front of the body

sources: Established S&C coaching literature (strongman conditioning texts, USAW technical manual for the Olympic-lift derivatives)
candidates.notes: Ballistic per EL-7 (throw); never_auto. Two common variants (forward soccer-style throw, backward-over-head heave) share this row per EL-2 (same implement, same overhead-release stimulus); aliases cover both. "medicine_ball" implement-set gap as above (overheadPosition itself derives correctly via the name).

candidates.name: Medicine Ball Scoop Toss

distinctFrom.why: power is generated from a squat-and-hip-extension scoop off the floor into the throw, rather than a standing rotational wind-up; the legs/hips are the prime mover, not the trunk rotation

sources: Established S&C coaching literature (strongman conditioning texts, USAW technical manual for the Olympic-lift derivatives)
candidates.notes: Ballistic per EL-7 (throw); never_auto. "medicine_ball" implement-set gap as above.

candidates.name: Hang Clean

distinctFrom.why: starts from a hang position above the knee rather than the floor, removing the first pull and floor pick-up phase

sources: Established S&C coaching literature (strongman conditioning texts, USAW technical manual for the Olympic-lift derivatives)
candidates.notes: Ballistic (clean); never_auto and difficulty 3 per the explicit brief instruction for Olympic-derived lifts.

candidates.name: Hang Snatch

distinctFrom.why: new movement family for this corpus: no full or hang snatch of any kind is seeded (only "Snatch Grip Deadlift" and "Snatch Grip Shrug" exist, neither of which catches the bar overhead)

sources: Established S&C coaching literature (strongman conditioning texts, USAW technical manual for the Olympic-lift derivatives)
candidates.notes: Ballistic (snatch); never_auto, difficulty 3 per the brief.

candidates.name: Snatch Pull

distinctFrom.why: snatch-width grip and pull to a higher finish (chest-high shrug) than the clean-width, lower-finishing clean pull

sources: Established S&C coaching literature (strongman conditioning texts, USAW technical manual for the Olympic-lift derivatives)
candidates.notes: Ballistic (a snatch derivative); never_auto, difficulty 3 per the brief. "Clean Pull" already exists as a seeded barbell row (hinge pattern), which is why this candidate is compared against it rather than added as a duplicate.

candidates.name: Push Jerk

distinctFrom.why: catches the bar overhead with a re-bend/dip of the knees (a jerk catch), rather than one continuous leg drive straight to lockout

sources: Established S&C coaching literature (strongman conditioning texts, USAW technical manual for the Olympic-lift derivatives)
candidates.notes: Ballistic (jerk); never_auto, difficulty 3 per the brief.

candidates.name: Split Jerk

distinctFrom.why: the feet split fore-aft to catch the bar overhead, rather than re-bending the knees in a parallel stance

sources: Established S&C coaching literature (strongman conditioning texts, USAW technical manual for the Olympic-lift derivatives)
candidates.notes: Ballistic (jerk); never_auto, difficulty 3 per the brief. Competition weightlifting jerk variant.

candidates.name: Muscle Snatch

distinctFrom.why: the bar is pressed/pulled straight through to lockout with no receiving dip under it, a strict-technique drill rather than the competition catch

sources: Established S&C coaching literature (strongman conditioning texts, USAW technical manual for the Olympic-lift derivatives)
candidates.notes: Ballistic (a snatch derivative used as a technique drill); never_auto, difficulty 3 per the brief.

candidates.name: Barbell High Pull

distinctFrom.why: pulled higher, to a high-elbow chest-height finish, rather than stopping at the shrug-height clean pull finish

sources: Established S&C coaching literature (strongman conditioning texts, USAW technical manual for the Olympic-lift derivatives)
candidates.notes: Ballistic (high pull); never_auto per the brief’s explicit "every high pull is never_auto" instruction.

rejected.name: Sandbag Carry
rejected.reason: not representable (no equipment vocabulary bucket fits a sandbag: it is neither a barbell/dumbbell/kettlebell-style rigid implement nor a medicine ball; forcing it into "medicine_ball" would misrepresent the unstable, shifting-load handling that is the whole point of the implement)

rejected.name: Bulgarian Bag Swing
rejected.reason: not representable (same equipment-vocabulary gap as the sandbag; also overlaps mechanically with the already-covered kettlebell swing family)

rejected.name: Plate Pinch Carry
rejected.reason: duplicate of 'Pinch Grip Carry' (already seeded, barbell equipment, carry pattern)

rejected.name: Clean Pull
rejected.reason: duplicate of 'Clean Pull' (already seeded, barbell equipment, hinge pattern)

rejected.name: Power Snatch
rejected.reason: out of this family’s assigned scope (a full barehand Olympic lift belongs with the barbell family’s own Olympic-lift coverage, not the carries/sleds/power inventory); flagged in the report as a corpus gap since only "Power Clean" is currently seeded and no barbell Snatch of any kind exists

rejected.name: Sled Sprint (Resisted)
rejected.reason: not distinct under EL-2 from a running/cardio modality (the brief explicitly rejects running); kept out to avoid re-introducing an endurance-adjacent logging case through the sled family

vocabularyGaps: No "distance" exerciseType exists in the schema (only weight_reps, duration, weighted_bodyweight); every carry/sled-drag candidate in this family needs one, and today the existing carry rows (Farmer’s Walk etc.) are seeded as weight_reps by convention rather than a true distance/time type. Flagged, not invented.
No equipment bucket fits a sandbag or a Bulgarian bag; both rejected as not representable under the closed equipment vocabulary.
No coarse equipment value exists for a trap/hex bar or other specialty bars (EL-4 buckets them under "barbell" by design; followed here for the Trap Bar Carry).
